title: Thy Presence, Ever Living God
description: Thy Presence, Ever Living God in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 67, “Christian Farewell”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thy pre-sence, ev-er liv-ing God! Wide through all na-ture spreads a-broad; Thy watch-ful eyes, which nev-er sleep, In ev-ery place Thy child-ren keep.

lines: Wide through all nature spreads abroad;
Thy watchful eyes, which never sleep,
In every place Thy children keep.
While near each other we remain,
Thou dost our lives and powers sustain;
When separate, we rejoice to share
Thy counsels, and Thy gracious care.
To Thee we now commit our ways,
And still implore Thy heavenly grace;
Still cause Thy face on us to shine,
And guard and guide us still as Thine.
Give us within Thy house to raise
Or, if that joy no more be known,
Give us to meet around Thy throne.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
